description: A well and settlement in Canaan's southern edge where Abraham made a covenant with Abimelech and named the site for their oath (Genesis 21:22-34), and where Isaac later dug his own well and renewed the same covenant (Genesis 26:23-33). "From Dan to Beersheba" became a standard phrase for the whole extent of Israel's territory (Judges 20:1). Elijah fled there, exhausted, after fleeing Jezebel's threat (1 Kings 19:3).
family_friendly_summary: Beersheba was a town at the southern edge of Israel, built around an important well. Abraham, and later his son Isaac, each made a peace agreement there. People said "from Dan to Beersheba" to mean the whole land of Israel, from top to bottom. Elijah once stopped in Beersheba when he was worn out and afraid.
